name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,207

clue.text: Means of communicating in Asia is part of our duties

indicators.note: something that is part of a phrase sits inside it, so the letters are lifted from within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A remark about a language used in Asia being part of one's responsibilities.
explanation.walkthrough: Read ouR DUties straight through, ignoring the space, and the language appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language spoken mainly in Pakistan and India, and a language is a means of communicating.

clue.text: World half united over poetry

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping only one of its two halves, here the front three of six letters

blocks.note: the first half of this six-letter word
verse is another word for poetry

explanation.surface: A grand claim that half the world was brought together by poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is all of existence, and 'world' is used loosely for everything there is.

clue.text: Greek character, model, talented to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so just a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A description of someone from Greece who is a model and fairly gifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' reads as a person from Greece, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet; moDEL TAlented hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character is a written symbol.

clue.text: Food item — mince on the outside — at formal event

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the two end letters of the word
taken as written
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A dish served at a formal function, with minced meat on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' suggests the meat itself, but only its outer letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is a small round of minced meat, a common item of food served in sauce or soup.

clue.text: Parent’s strange catch

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual shape, so these letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark about a mother or father's odd way of catching something.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is': the parent is strange, so its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to snare or trick them, which is to catch them out.

clue.text: Personality name — pet term at work

indicators.note: letters at work are being busily handled and reshaped rather than left in place

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's pet name used in the office says something about their personality.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words between the dash and the indicator supply exactly eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperament is a person's characteristic nature and moods, a close synonym of personality.

clue.text: Cross as nothing new organised, you’re extremely disappointed at the outset

indicators.note: to organise is to put things into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are reordered
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters survive
the outset is the very start, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the opening letter of this little word
no, as in no thing at all
N is the standard abbreviation for new
first and last letters of the contraction
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Angry because nothing new has been set up, you are very let down from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: the A seems to come from the start of 'as' with no signal of its own. The rest is ANNO, then YE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross is an informal adjective meaning angry or irritated, the same state as being annoyed.

clue.text: Lean record

blocks.note: first meaning: to tilt to one side, as a ship does
second meaning: a written series of items

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like an adjective for thin meat, but here it is a verb for tilting, as a damaged ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans to one side is said to have a tilt that way, and a set of names written down forms a register.

clue.text: One will insist at beginning city mainly wrong

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken
mainly means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the contracted form, as in I'll
the first letter of the word
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone declares from the start that the city is mostly in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One will' reads as a phrase but gives I and 'LL, the clipped form of will, making I'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illicit is forbidden by law or custom, so it is improper or not right.

clue.text: Helpful to cover a pie somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified manner, so the letters may come out in any order

blocks.note: all eleven letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Advice that it helps to put a lid of pastry over a pie in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture hides that the whole phrase after the definition is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooperative person willingly assists and works along with others, which is being helpful.

clue.text: Sign, first of many in America

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter
taken as written
the United States

explanation.surface: A sign seen as the first of many such signs across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a placing word, but it is simply part of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: The minus is the arithmetic symbol for subtraction, one of the mathematical signs.

clue.text: Real tale boy revised in complex way

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A true story about a boy rewritten in an intricate fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The story setting makes 'revised' look like an editor's word, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Done elaborately means done with many detailed parts, which is an intricate or complicated manner.

clue.text: Irish XV listener recollected

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered up again into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irish rugby team is remembered by someone who was listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' means remembered on the surface; split as re-collected it means gathered again. Leinster is one of Ireland's provincial rugby union sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team fields fifteen players, so an Irish XV can be the provincial side from that eastern province.

clue.text: Fish in tin moved to and fro

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the second piece wraps the first

blocks.note: hake is a sea fish
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A fish in a can that has been rattled back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin' suggests a can of fish, but it is the element, whose symbol comes from Latin stannum.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaken is the past participle of shake, meaning jolted rapidly back and forth.

clue.text: Legal case about university sale

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: an action is a lawsuit
U is a standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A lawsuit concerning the sale of a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning' on the surface, but it signals going around.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Initially challenged at debate, stop working as club advisor

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: Someone first challenged in a debate quits their post advising a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a society with an advisor, but it is a golf club, and the advisor carries the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's clubs and advises on which club to choose and how to play.

clue.text: Not entirely loyal worker? He doesn’t turn up

indicators.note: not entirely means falling short of whole, so the word is cut by its last letter

blocks.note: true, meaning loyal, minus its final letter
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: An employee whose loyalty is partial, so perhaps he skips work.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the first half; the second sentence is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant stays away from school or work without permission, so is someone absent when expected.

clue.text: One running meeting — no fan of standing?

blocks.note: first meaning: whoever presides over a gathering
second meaning, playful: someone devoted to seats rather than staying on their feet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests a race, but it means presiding. The second half reads the answer literally as a person keen on seats, and the question mark flags that whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who presides over a committee or board conducts its business, and literally could be someone fond of seats.

clue.text: Money risked in post

blocks.note: first meaning: a sum wagered on an outcome
second meaning: a pointed wooden pole driven into the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Money risked in post' sounds like cash sent by mail, but 'post' is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler's wager is called this, and so is a sharpened wooden pole hammered into earth.

clue.text: Powder story is given new ending

indicators.note: a new ending replaces the old last letter with a different one

blocks.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A story about powder gets a fresh conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says only that the last letter changes, not which letter replaces it; the crossing letter from 22 Across supplies the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine powder used on skin.

clue.text: Bail arranged before one’s evidence about location

indicators.note: arranged means put into order, here an order different from the given one

blocks.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I; the apostrophe-s is absorbed

explanation.surface: A court scene: bail is set before someone's evidence of where they were.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'Bail' look like part of the story, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim, with proof, that the accused was somewhere else when the crime happened.

clue.text: Charm a non-drinker right before performance

blocks.note: taken as written
TT stands for teetotal
R is the abbreviation for right
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Win over a teetotaller just before a show.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, is how crosswords write someone who never drinks alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to draw them in with appeal, which is what it means to attract them.

clue.text: Piece of music, caught in the past, retro, regularly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals drops every other letter, keeping the rest

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
once means at some former time
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A piece of music, caught in some old retro style, keeps being overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught in' looks like a container, but caught is just C, and 'in the past' is a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical composition for a solo instrument with an orchestra.

clue.text: Tolerate gradual impairment from use

blocks.note: first meaning: to accept or put up with, as in 'he won't stand for it'
second meaning: the damage that builds up through use

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is informal, mostly British: 'the boss won't wear it' means will not accept it.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, to put up with an idea is to accept it, and the noun names the slow deterioration of things in use.
